q: Do you know which interpreter receives the value?
why: Every injection class is defined by its sink, and the payload is a consequence of the sink. Choosing a payload before a sink is how scanners produce false positives.

branches.action: find the sink first. arithmetic or syntax that only one interpreter evaluates beats a payload list
branches.oracle: a response only that interpreter could produce

branches.action: read the handlers, pick a context payload, confirm with a callback under a control
boolean and time based pairs, never a destructive statement
branches.oracle: differential or timing with a matched control

branches.action: blind time based first, then a reversible side effect
branches.oracle: timing control plus a benign artefact

branches.action: identify the sink and the classpath, then match a gadget
store then trigger a different read. the oracle is in the second request
branches.oracle: effect appears on a later read
